slides.title: Which inline speed frame should you buy?
slides.sub: Five checks before you order your next frame

slides.title: Check mounting first
slides.body: Bolt spacing is the one thing that can stop a frame fitting your boots at all. Measure front bolt to rear bolt: 150, 165 or 195mm.

slides.title: Choose your wheel size
slides.caption: Smaller wheels turn and accelerate quickly, bigger wheels roll further per stride.

slides.title: Three wheels or four
slides.body: Four wheels give grip and a planted race feel. A triskate turns more willingly and still rolls fast on big wheels.

slides.title: Length sets the character
slides.body: A long frame tracks straight and stays calm at race pace. A short frame turns eagerly and feels lively underfoot.

slides.title: Fit it to your boot
slides.body: Under a small boot, a long frame sticks out past the toe and heel. That overhang is what catches when you lean hard into a corner.

slides.text: Get the frame right and everything above it works better.
